title: Israel Camped as One
hookLine: the Jewish people as one, beyond every movement
carry: klal yisrael: one people, wider than any stream

cards: "And all the people answered together." That's the book of Exodus, at the foot of Mount Sinai. A crowd of former slaves, tired, unsure, some of them already complaining, and the text says they answered together.
Not the elders for them. Not the best of them. All.

This block has counted streams: Orthodox and Haredi, Conservative and Reform, Reconstructionist, Renewal, Humanistic, secular, traditional, no label at all. Today steps back far enough to see them as one thing.

teach.b: Klal Yisrael. Klal means the whole, the general, everything together. Yisrael is Israel, the people.
The whole people. Four turns. First, the camp.
Earlier in the same chapter: "there Israel camped before the mount." The medieval commentator Rashi noticed that the Hebrew verb is singular: Israel camped, as one, like one person with one heart.
On other days in the desert they quarreled. At Sinai they camped as one. Second, the answer: "All that the LORD hath spoken we will do."
The covenant is made with a people, not a club of the most devoted. Third, what the phrase does today.
Klal Yisrael points at something wider than any movement: the Jew in a black hat and the Jew who hasn't been to synagogue in years, the Jews of Morocco and Ukraine, of Ethiopia and Ohio.
The arguments of this block happen inside a family, not between strangers. Fourth, the pull it creates.
Some Jews feel it as a reason to keep a practice, so that Jews elsewhere can eat at their table or count them in their prayer. Others feel it as a reason to show up when Jews far away are in trouble.
Different streams draw different lines on many questions.
Klal Yisrael is the circle drawn around all of the lines.

how: Jews speak of klal Yisrael when they act for the Jewish people as a whole: supporting Jews in other countries, keeping practices that let others join them, and praying for Jews they will never meet.

games.q: you're at the foot of Sinai with a crowd that has complained its way through the desert. who does the text say answered?
o: the elders and the most devoted.
games.why: "and all the people answered together": the covenant is made with the whole people.

practice: If you're Jewish, picture someone of your people who lives differently, another stream, country or language, another way of keeping Shabbat or not keeping it, and give them a face, a kitchen, a morning.

If you're not Jewish, picture someone in your own community who prays, votes or lives very differently from you. Hold them in mind without arguing, as part of the whole, and if you pray, include them in your prayer.
